newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Feb 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian swimmer Michael Klim lowered his national 200 metre freestyle record to 1 minute, 45.34 seconds at the World Cup meet in Gelsenkirchen yesterday. The 19-year-old has beaten that record three times in the last six weeks, but finished third in th 100 metre butterfly. Page 14.

Tasmania will almost certainly defeat South Australia in the Sheffield Shield cricket match at Adelaide Oval this morning. Tasmania took a first innings lead of 132 and have South Australia six wickets for 127 in their second innings. Page 14.

The Australian Olympic Committee wants fixed selection policies in all its member sports federations by the end of this year. The Committee wants to avoid legal disputes over selection at the Sydney Olympics following selection difficulties at the AtlantaOlympics. Page 14.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia lost the fifth cricket test to the West Indies in Perth yesterday by 10 wickets, but retained the Frank Worrell Trophy, taking the series 3-2. The Australians were bowled out in their second innings for 194, leaving the West Indies a 57 run chas for victory. The Aussies collapsed in their second innings for 194 as West Indian bowler Courtney Walsh took five wickets. Page 40.

Australian sprint hurdle legend Shirley (Strickland) de la Hunty is back coaching at the age of 70. The former Olympic medallist is teaching five hurdlers in Perth to compete against the nation's best. De la Hunty won seven medals from three consecutive Olympic games. Page 39.

The Australian Rugby League will almost certainly seek an injunction to stop some players joining Super League after signing loyalty contracts, but may grant others a reprieve. Brisbane recruit Anthony Mundine and five Penrith players may play in Super Legue's opening rounds. Page 39.
THE AGE

Australian cycling team manager Mike Turtur claims former champion Kathy Watt made no attempt to put herself in a winning position in the defence of her road race title at the Atlanta Olympics. In his official review of the team. Turtur also claims Watts' management undermined her chances of winning by encouraging her to compete in more events. Page C6.

Formula One racing cars will not be tested on Australia's Phillip Island before next month's Grand Prix in Melbourne. The Formula One Constructors Association ruled out using the track between 26 February and 2 March to test the cars, opting for Kyalami in South Africa instead. Page C6.

Australian Football League club Carlton is leading a push to replace long-serving commissioner Graeme Samuel with tribunal chairman Neil Busse on the four person League Commission. Five candidates are fighting for the positions, with Carlton calling for new blood." Page C6.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian golfer Greg Norman says he feels sorry 21-year-old Tiger Woods because of the pressures of his success. Norman says Woods has a lot on his plate and must carry many responsibilities in representing minority groups. Woods comes to Melbourne next week to appear as a celebrity guest at the Australian Masters at Huntingdale. Page 70.

Melbourne's autumn racing carnival was launched yesterday, with the top trainers and jockeys of the industry in City Square. The A$1.2 million Australian Cup and the A$350,000 Cadbury Guineas will be the highlight races of the carnival. Page 66.

The Australian Football League has announced a total operating revenue of A$74.274 million for 1996, up almost A$7 million from the previous year. The League produced an operating surplus of A$38.7 million, of which A$30.548 million was paid to the clubs. Page 70.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The New South Wales TAB, the world's largest off-course betting operation, may be corporatised by June this year under a state government scheme to revive the industry. According to The Daily Telegraph, the government also plans to increase the number of Sunday race dates and introduce a standard promotional system for the industry. Page 58.

Australia fared well in a sport-by-sport ranking based on performances at the Atlanta Olympics. Australia were No 1 in the world in hockey and rowing, and second in swimming. Points were awarded for top eight finishes at the Games. Page 58.

According to French Cup captain Yannick Noah, Australia may include Todd Woodbridge as a singles tennis player in their Davis Cup team. The French team play Australia at White City in Sydney this weekend, with the Australian team having until Thursday morning to choose a team. Page 54.
